_comment: Executable claims for OPEN-DECISIONS.md, one JSON object per line. `status` is the state of THIS CLAIM, not of the whole OD entry — an entry can be partly resolved (OD-56's Python half is fixed while its Node transitives are not, so its aiohttp/cryptography claim is `resolved` while OD-56 itself stays open). resolved = the claim MUST hold; if it stops holding, the fix regressed. open = the claim must NOT hold yet; if it starts holding, strike that part of the entry off. See scripts/check_decision_claims.sh and CLAUDE.md §5b.

claim: analytics.controller.ts is guarded (no longer an unauthenticated paid-LLM surface)
jwt-secret.ts throws rather than falling back to a published string
SimposController is guarded AND SimposModule stays gated out of production
no bare fetch() of a user-supplied URL remains in vendor-page-extractor — both sites go through safeFetch
splitPdfIfLarge caps pages, so chunk count cannot track an uploaded PDF's page count
the four pos_* tables carry foreign keys (was 3, now 13)
aiohttp and cryptography are pinned at or above their patched versions (the Python half of OD-56; the Node transitives are separate and still open)
verify: python3 -c "import re,sys; s=open('services/agent-orchestrator/requirements.txt').read(); a=re.search(r'^aiohttp==(\\S+)',s,re.M).group(1); c=re.search(r'^cryptography==(\\S+)',s,re.M).group(1); v=lambda x:[int(n) for n in x.split('.')]; sys.exit(0 if v(a)>=[3,14,3] and v(c)>=[50,0,0] else 1)"

claim: calendar_agent's regex fallback is NOT fed the prompt template (fixed in #57; the separate question of provider_important_dates not existing in production is OD-68)
verify: python3 -c "import re,sys; s=open('services/agent-orchestrator/agents/calendar_agent.py').read(); sys.exit(1 if re.search(r'_regex_date_extraction\\(\\s*prompt\\s*\\)', s) else 0)"

claim: no file in apps/web/src imports the browser anon-key Supabase client any more (OD-45 removed useReportQueries; useSommelierQueries is the last one). Holds when the sommelier surface is routed through the gateway, or when the hook is deleted
a migration revokes anon's DML on the procurement document tables, so the invoice store is not readable/writable with the public anon key
verify: python3 -c "import glob,re,sys; pat=re.compile(r'revoke\s+all[^;]*\bprocurement_documents\b[^;]*\bfrom\b[^;]*\banon\b',re.I|re.S); sys.exit(0 if [f for f in glob.glob('supabase/migrations/*.sql') if pat.search(open(f,errors='ignore').read())] else 1)"

claim: document_extraction grades itself: the reconciliation verdict is wired from applyTieOut into nf_verdict, invoices only
nf_verdict ships with RLS enabled and anon/authenticated revoked in its CREATING migration, not a follow-up
verify: grep -q 'alter table public.nf_verdict enable row level security' supabase/migrations/20260825180000_nf_verdict.sql && grep -q 'revoke all on public.nf_verdict from anon, authenticated' supabase/migrations/20260825180000_nf_verdict.sql

claim: the verified-cost readout GROUPS by basis rather than filtering, so two graders can never average into one figure
the tie-out tolerance has one definition, shared by the grader and the evidence it records
the Python emitter returns the inserted NF row id, so a verdict can attach to it
rfq_agent stamps a parse-level basis rather than asserting success above the parse
the spine names exactly one current milestone — P2 — in all three docs
verify: grep -q 'Current milestone: P2' .planning/STATE.md && grep -q 'Current Milestone: P2' .planning/PROJECT.md && grep -q '## Now — P2' .planning/ROADMAP.md

claim: every page note in 06-pages carries a Surface section (the page graph is complete)
no web source navigates to the dead routes /documents or /emails
verify: test "$(grep -rn "'/documents'\|\"/documents\"\|'/emails'\|\"/emails\"" apps/web/src --include='*.tsx' --include='*.ts' | grep -v documents-reports | wc -l | tr -d ' ')" = 0

claim: the tenant comparison runs inside JwtAuthGuard, where request.user exists
the communications test/e2e routes are unreachable in production
apps/web/src/types/companyClass.ts is deleted and types/index.ts no longer re-exports it
verify: test -f apps/web/src/types/index.ts && test ! -f apps/web/src/types/companyClass.ts && ! grep -q companyClass apps/web/src/types/index.ts

claim: the three dead exports are gone from apps/web/src/data/customEventTypes.ts while the module and isEventTypeNameAvailable survive
verify: test -f apps/web/src/data/customEventTypes.ts && grep -q 'export function isEventTypeNameAvailable' apps/web/src/data/customEventTypes.ts && ! grep -qE 'export (function isCustomEventType|function getCustomEventTypeByName|const EVENT_TYPE_COLORS)' apps/web/src/data/customEventTypes.ts

claim: Gmail push enforcement is on — either the Pub/Sub pair or the REQUIRE flag is committed to an env template
the staged-open Gmail path still counts and logs every unverified push
the schema-wide revoke migration is present and asserts its own outcome
verify: grep -q 'alter default privileges' supabase/migrations/20260825210000_od72_revoke_client_grants.sql && grep -q 'OD-72 not closed' supabase/migrations/20260825210000_od72_revoke_client_grants.sql

claim: the anon-DML migration is present and asserts its own outcome
the Python emit sites stamp the parse-level basis rather than call-level
the reports palette cannot return a fabricated answer — the mock generator is gone
verify: test "$(grep -rE 'function generateMockAnswer|const generateMockAnswer' apps/web/src --include='*.tsx' --include='*.ts' | grep -v '__tests__' | wc -l | tr -d ' ')" = 0

claim: every studio call goes through the gateway on a relative path (the founder chose the gateway proxy over the direct-to-orchestrator base URL; supersedes OD-82's inverse claim)
the vision extractor stamps restaurant_id on its spend rows, so the per-restaurant cap can match
the feature-flag registry is the single source naming which flags are real
the autonomous-send switch is surfaced in the settings UI
the weekly manager email no longer carries hard-coded top-seller figures
the dashboard day-detail modal labels vendor spend as spend, not revenue
verify: test "$(grep -c '>Total Revenue<' apps/web/src/pages/Dashboard.tsx)" = 0 && grep -q '>Vendor Spend<' apps/web/src/pages/Dashboard.tsx

claim: /receiving is reachable from the sidebar, not URL-only
redeem_invite is not gated on a studio role
redeem_invite binds the grant to the invite's target_email
target_email is required at mint, so an unbound token cannot be created
token consumption is a conditional update, not a racy read-then-write
the web app has a /studio/invite/:token route that is not studio-role gated
the gateway routes /api/v1/studio/* to the orchestrator with the caller's own token
the gateway serves the onboarding extract route, so studio ingestion survives the move to relative paths
the mock-only e2e studio tests run without production Supabase credentials
booting the gateway outside production no longer rewrites the committed openapi.json as a side effect
the committed openapi.json matches the routes the code actually serves (pos-hub sale-unit routes present)
the gateway emails the studio invite instead of returning the link, and the token is absent from the success response
StudioInviteController is registered before StudioProxyController, so the wildcard cannot swallow POST /studio/invite
verify: python3 -c "import re,sys; s=open('apps/api-gateway/src/common/orchestrator/orchestrator.module.ts').read(); i=s.find('StudioInviteController,'); p=s.find('StudioProxyController,'); sys.exit(0 if i!=-1 and p!=-1 and i

claim: the studio proxy refuses a wildcard path that escapes the /studio/ prefix, so it cannot be used as a generic authenticated proxy into the orchestrator
the JWT subject is escaped before it reaches a log line (CodeQL py/log-injection alert 884)

the gateway serves POST /api/v1/onboarding/extract: OnboardingProxyController declares the route, is registered in OrchestratorModule under the api/v1 global prefix, and the orchestrator it forwards to still declares the matching /extract route
verify: grep -q '@Post("extract")' apps/api-gateway/src/common/orchestrator/onboarding-proxy.controller.ts && grep -q '@Controller("onboarding")' apps/api-gateway/src/common/orchestrator/onboarding-proxy.controller.ts && grep -q 'OnboardingProxyController,' apps/api-gateway/src/common/orchestrator/orchestrator.module.ts && grep -q 'setGlobalPrefix("api/v1")' apps/api-gateway/src/main.ts && grep -q '@router.post("/extract")' services/agent-orchestrator/api/onboarding_routes.py

claim: the agent-health lookup validates its path segment, so an escaped path cannot carry X-Admin-Key out of the health prefix
the Toast menu and order lookups validate their ids before interpolating them into an orchestrator URL
all three flagged onboarding log sites escape their request-derived value, and the unsanitizable f-string form is gone
verify: test "$(grep -c 'sanitize_for_log(' services/agent-orchestrator/api/onboarding_routes.py)" -ge 3 && ! grep -q 'f"All pages failed for restaurant' services/agent-orchestrator/api/onboarding_routes.py

claim: getProfileForUser (the /auth/me source) returns emailVerified — the field ProtectedRoute compares
verify: python3 -c "import sys;s=open('apps/api-gateway/src/auth/auth.service.ts').read();i=s.find('async getProfileForUser');b=s[i:i+1600];sys.exit(0 if i!=-1 and 'emailVerified:' in b else 1)"

claim: JwtStrategy.validate carries emailVerified onto request.user, so a server-side check has something to read
verify: python3 -c "import sys;s=open('apps/api-gateway/src/auth/strategies/jwt.strategy.ts').read();i=s.find('async validate');sys.exit(0 if i!=-1 and 'emailVerified:' in s[i:] else 1)"

claim: JwtAuthGuard actually CALLS assertEmailVerified — the check is wired, not merely defined (the tenant-guard failure mode)
assertEmailVerified fails CLOSED on a missing field: it requires === true rather than testing for === false
the scheduled crons iterate restaurants instead of reading one DEFAULT_RESTAURANT_ID
no scheduled-tasks email hard-codes the restaurant name; each names its own tenant
non-legacy tenants cannot fall back to the global MANAGER_EMAIL — the resolver honours allowDefaultFallback
the tenant-scoped crons honour each restaurant's own timezone instead of a pinned America/New_York

no report surface offers a control that can only fail: DocumentsPage exports reportFileUnavailableReason and no longer alerts 'No file available', and Communications no longer defines handleGenerateReportNow
verify: grep -q 'export function reportFileUnavailableReason' apps/web/src/pages/DocumentsPage.tsx && test "$(grep -cE '^[^*]*[^a-zA-Z.]alert\(' apps/web/src/pages/DocumentsPage.tsx)" = 0 && test "$(grep -c 'const handleGenerateReportNow' apps/web/src/pages/Communications.tsx)" = 0

claim: a failed schedule read is rendered as a failure, not as emptiness: ReportScheduler declares a schedulesError prop and Communications sets it in the catch
generated_reports has a producer: ReportsService (the only file in the repo that touches the table) contains an .update( call that could advance a row off status pending
the log-injection sweep is in place across the orchestrator, not confined to the three sites first reported
no sanitized (string) value is fed to a numeric %-format spec — logging would trap the TypeError and silently lose the line rather than raise

the three surviving py/log-injection alerts are all false positives that need a CodeQL dismissal, not code: two in snapshots.py (archetype_id gated to literal JSONL_SOURCES keys) and admin_routes library_tier (an int post-Pydantic-validation)
verify: ! grep -q 'sanitize_for_log' scripts/synth/snapshots.py && grep -q 'Unknown archetype for refresh' scripts/synth/snapshots.py && grep -q 'library_tier: int = Field(ge=0, le=4' services/agent-orchestrator/api/admin_routes.py

claim: integration_oauth_connections and integration_oauth_states are created by a migration in supabase/migrations/, the directory that is applied, not only in migrations_archive/ which is not
verify: grep -rqiE "create table (if not exists )?(public\.)?integration_oauth_connections" supabase/migrations/ && grep -rqiE "create table (if not exists )?(public\.)?integration_oauth_states" supabase/migrations/

claim: RLS and the anon/authenticated REVOKE live in the SAME migration that creates each table, not a follow-up - these tables hold OAuth refresh tokens
verify: test -n "$(grep -rliE "create table (if not exists )?public\.integration_oauth_connections" supabase/migrations/)" && test "$(grep -rliE "create table (if not exists )?public\.integration_oauth_connections" supabase/migrations/)" = "$(grep -rliE "revoke all on public\.integration_oauth_connections from anon, authenticated" supabase/migrations/)" && test "$(grep -rliE "create table (if not exists )?public\.integration_oauth_states" supabase/migrations/)" = "$(grep -rliE "revoke all on public\.integration_oauth_states from anon, authenticated" supabase/migrations/)"

claim: UNIQUE (user_id, integration_id) has no WHERE predicate, so storeConnection's PostgREST upsert onConflict can bind to it (comments stripped first, so the header prose explaining the rule cannot satisfy the grep)
the creating migration asserts its own outcome in a DO block, including that anon holds no privilege on either table
the integrations module has a spec that binds every table the service queries to an applied migration, and it fails when that migration is absent
verify: test -f apps/api-gateway/src/integrations/integrations-oauth.service.spec.ts && grep -q "backed by an applied migration" apps/api-gateway/src/integrations/integrations-oauth.service.spec.ts

claim: the push-subscription read checks `error` instead of discarding it — a PostgREST failure can no longer become an empty recipient list
no migration creates push_subscriptions — the table is deliberately absent, not pending
every notification_agent push call site goes through _push_targets, so an unreadable source records a failed leg rather than silently skipping
pushSubscriptionIds is no longer dead — either a caller outside the resolver reads it, or the field has been removed (OD-95 fork)
verify: test "$(grep -rl 'pushSubscriptionIds' apps --include='*.ts' | grep -v node_modules | grep -vE 'recipient-resolver\.service\.ts|scheduled-tasks\.service\.ts|\.spec\.ts' | wc -l | tr -d ' ')" != 0

claim: the identity provider registry is a single definition declaring password, google, microsoft and apple — adding a provider is an entry in it
verify: grep -q "export const IDENTITY_PROVIDERS" apps/api-gateway/src/auth/identity-providers.ts && grep -q 'id: "apple"' apps/api-gateway/src/auth/identity-providers.ts && grep -q 'id: "microsoft"' apps/api-gateway/src/auth/identity-providers.ts && grep -q "export function defaultSignInMethods" apps/api-gateway/src/auth/identity-providers.ts

claim: validateUser reads linked providers from user_oauth_accounts and has an honest NO_SIGNIN_METHOD answer for an account with none
verify: grep -q "async resolveLinkedProviderIds" apps/api-gateway/src/auth/auth.service.ts && grep -q 'code: "NO_SIGNIN_METHOD"' apps/api-gateway/src/auth/auth.service.ts && grep -q 'from("user_oauth_accounts")' apps/api-gateway/src/auth/auth.service.ts

claim: no provider name is inferred from users.oauth_provider anywhere in auth.service.ts (comment lines stripped first, so the note explaining the removal cannot satisfy the grep)
the identity-resolution endpoint is rate limited by a decorator attached to that handler, not merely present somewhere in the file
requestPasswordReset stays enumeration-safe — this ADR reveals methods on the sign-in route and must never be used to weaken the reset route
verify: grep -q "async requestPasswordReset" apps/api-gateway/src/auth/auth.service.ts && grep -q "If an account exists for that email" apps/api-gateway/src/auth/auth.controller.ts

claim: the login page renders resolved methods and no longer shortcuts gmail addresses into Google before trying a password
